competency_fulfillment.rationale: Three of the four named terms are tested through direct definitional questions (seed 42 for point, seed 44 for line, seed 45 for ray), but no sample tests 'line segment', and none present a 'using models' visual-recognition or 'draws' production task -- all five are text-only 'what do we call' MCQs.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: 'Line segment' is one of the four terms explicitly named in the competency text and it never appears in any of the five samples; meanwhile the point question, 'an exact location in space with no length or width', is repeated in seeds 43 and 46 with only the option order changed.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The definitional language used, such as 'no length or width', 'extends forever in both directions', and 'one endpoint', is precise and appropriately simple for grade-3 quarter-1 geometry vocabulary.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only three distinct questions exist across five samples (point, line, ray), with the point question alone accounting for 3 of the 5 seeds, so effectively 60% of the batch is redundant rather than varied.

competency_alignment.rationale: Repeating the identical point-definition question three times (seeds 42, 43, 46) doesn't build coverage of the other three named terms, so the batch's variation skews toward one term instead of the competency's full four-term scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: There is no numeric range at stake for this qualitative-definition competency, and the vocabulary complexity used, e.g. 'endpoint' and 'extends forever', is not inflated beyond grade-3 level.
